newsitem.title: UK: UK's Sedgwick profits up on lower turnover.
newsitem.headline: UK's Sedgwick profits up on lower turnover.

text.p: Boosted by improved business in the United States, British insurance broker Sedgwick Group Plc reported first half pre-tax profits at the top end of market expectations at 66.5 million pounds ($105.2 million) against 64.1 million the previous year.
The group's main business covering brokerage and fees, however, dipped marginally to 465.4 million pounds from 467.3 million.
At constant exchange rates, brokerage and frees improved by six percent. Trading profit for the group which excludes interest income was 49.0 million pounds, rising from 43.8 million.
The group's total turnover was 485 million pounds against 490.2 in 1996.
The group proposed an interim dividend of three pence a share -- unchanged from last year -- and said it would be paid as foreign income dividend.
The group's earnings per share rose to 8.4 pence from 7.8 pence.
Sedgwick said earnings were adversely affected by the strength of the sterling, which wiped seven million pounds from the profit total.
"Most of the foreign exchange impact for 1997 will have occurred in the first half of this year if sterling continues at current levels," it said.
Sedgwick's pre-market share price was marked two pence up to 121p by 0725 GMT.
